Routing notes:
- Option C is invalid for these requests, even when displayed as “regional office” or similar. Do not select C.
- Valid choices observed are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk).
- No successful examples establish when to choose A versus B.
- Request attributes seen: type (claim, shipment, invoice, refund), region (north/south/east), size (small/large), sender department, and message context. None has yet been confirmed as the routing rule.
- Avoid assuming that region, size, urgency wording, repeated attempts, or sender department alone determines A/B; seek additional evidence or use the explicit workflow rule if available.

Routing notes:
- Earlier assumption that option C is invalid is contradicted by new evidence. Do not rule out C; it is now the leading candidate.
- In REQ-2410–REQ-2416 and REQ-2418–REQ-2419, A (standard queue) was rejected.
- In REQ-2417, B (priority desk) was rejected.
- Thus, all tested A/B selections in these examples failed; no successful A or B example is established.
- C is consistently presented as “regional” or “regional office” (sometimes truncated), and should be tested/selected when available unless an explicit workflow rule says otherwise.
- The new failures span shipment, claim, refund, and invoice requests; north, east, and south regions; small and large sizes; and multiple departments. These attributes alone are not confirmed as the rule.
- Urgency wording, repeated attempts, sender department, size, request type, and region remain unproven as independent routing criteria.
- Prefer the explicit workflow rule if available; otherwise use C provisionally and continue collecting successful outcomes.

Routing notes:
- The prior assumption that C is generally valid/leading is contradicted. C was rejected in every new case REQ-2420–REQ-2429, all involving the north region.
- C was rejected across claim, refund, and shipment requests; small and large sizes; varied urgency wording; and multiple departments/senders. These attributes do not explain the failures independently.
- In REQ-2410–REQ-2416 and REQ-2418–REQ-2419, A (standard queue) was rejected; in REQ-2417, B (priority desk) was rejected. No successful A, B, or C example is established.
- Do not select C provisionally, especially for north-region requests. Treat its “regional office” label as descriptive, not evidence that it is valid.
- The evidence may indicate an unobserved rule involving region or another interaction, but does not establish the rule. North is now a strong warning signal for C; do not generalize this to other regions without evidence.
- Some prompts truncate or omit options. Select only an option explicitly available in the current prompt; never assume a missing option is valid.
- Prefer an explicit workflow rule if available. Otherwise, avoid confident routing based solely on request type, urgency wording, size, department, sender, or region, and continue collecting outcomes.

Routing notes:
- C is not generally valid. It was rejected in all north-region cases REQ-2420–REQ-2429 and again REQ-2430–REQ-2435, across claim, refund, and shipment contexts, sizes, urgency wording, and departments/senders.
- Do not select C provisionally, especially for north-region requests. “Regional office” is descriptive, not evidence of validity.
- A and B still have no broad rule or established general success. B succeeded once for REQ-2436 (east, large refund, urgent wording). No successful A example is established.
- The earlier assumption that only explicitly displayed options may be selected needs qualification: D was accepted for REQ-2432 (south invoice), REQ-2437, and REQ-2438, even though D was omitted from the visibly listed options. D was rejected as invalid in REQ-2430, REQ-2431, REQ-2433–REQ-2435, and REQ-2439 when attempted. Option truncation/availability is therefore significant; do not infer a universal D rule, but recognize that an omitted D may sometimes be valid.
- REQ-2437–2438 show D accepted for north shipment requests despite C being absent/truncated, so “north always rejects D” is not established. REQ-2432 shows D accepted in south; REQ-2439 shows D rejected in east.
- Avoid confident routing based solely on request type, urgency, size, department, sender, or region. Prefer an explicit workflow rule and inspect the complete current option list when possible; otherwise continue collecting outcomes.

Routing notes:
- C is not generally valid. It was rejected in all tested north-region cases (REQ-2420–REQ-2429, REQ-2430–REQ-2435, REQ-2441–REQ-2443, REQ-2446), across claim, refund, and shipment contexts, sizes, wording, and departments. Do not select C provisionally; “regional office” is descriptive, not proof of validity.
- A has no successful example and was rejected in REQ-2441–REQ-2447, including north and east refunds/shipments and varied sizes. Do not treat it as a safe default.
- B is not broadly valid. It was rejected for large east shipment requests REQ-2440 and REQ-2448. It succeeded for large east refunds with urgency/follow-up language in REQ-2436 (“urgent”) and REQ-2449 (“asking ... twice already”). This suggests urgency may matter for some refund cases, but is not yet a general rule.
- The earlier assumption that only visibly listed options may be selected is disproven: D was accepted for REQ-2432, REQ-2437, and REQ-2438 despite omission/truncation, but rejected in REQ-2430, REQ-2431, REQ-2433–REQ-2435, and REQ-2439. Omitted-option availability is significant, with no universal D rule.
- D can be valid for north shipment requests (REQ-2437–2438), so north does not imply D rejection; it was also accepted in south and rejected in east.
- Avoid routing solely by region, request type, urgency, size, department, sender, or wording. Prefer an explicit workflow rule and inspect the complete current option list when possible. If options are truncated or no rule is available, continue collecting outcomes rather than guessing.

Routing notes:
- C is not generally valid. It was rejected in all tested north-region cases (REQ-2420–REQ-2429, REQ-2430–REQ-2435, REQ-2441–REQ-2443, REQ-2446). “Regional office” is descriptive, not proof of validity. Do not select C provisionally.
- A has no successful example and was rejected in REQ-2441–REQ-2447 and REQ-2457, covering multiple regions, request types, sizes, and wording. Do not use it as a safe default.
- B is not broadly valid: it was rejected for large east shipments (REQ-2440, REQ-2448), but accepted for large east refunds with urgency/follow-up (REQ-2436, REQ-2449), a small east refund with deadline language (REQ-2459), a large north claim with repeated follow-up (REQ-2450), and a large north refund (REQ-2455). B may be favored for some non-shipment cases, especially with urgency or follow-up, but this is not a universal rule.
- D remains context-dependent. It was accepted for north shipments (REQ-2437–2438, REQ-2454, REQ-2456) and a large east shipment (REQ-2451), including varied wording and omitted/truncated listings. It was rejected for north refunds (REQ-2452, REQ-2458) and a north claim (REQ-2453), as well as earlier north/east cases. Shipment context currently provides the strongest D signal; do not generalize beyond it.
- The assumption that only visibly listed options may be selected is disproven: D was accepted despite omission/truncation, but omitted-option availability is not universal.
- Avoid routing solely by region, request type, urgency, size, department, sender, or wording. Prefer an explicit workflow rule and inspect the complete current option list. If no rule is available, continue collecting outcomes rather than guessing.

Routing notes:
- C has no successful example and was rejected across many north cases (REQ-2420–REQ-2435, REQ-2441–REQ-2443, REQ-2446) and related tests. “Regional office” wording is not proof of validity. Do not select C provisionally.
- A has no successful example and was rejected across multiple regions, request types, sizes, and wording (including REQ-2441–REQ-2447, REQ-2457). Do not use as a default.
- D is strongly associated with shipment requests: accepted for north shipments (REQ-2437–2438, REQ-2454, REQ-2456), large and small east shipments (REQ-2451, REQ-2463–2466), and varied urgency/wording. Shipment size, region, urgency, and “regional office” wording did not change this signal. Do not generalize D to other request types.
- B has several accepted refund cases (REQ-2436, REQ-2449, REQ-2450, REQ-2455, REQ-2459, REQ-2460, REQ-2462), including north refunds and both small/large cases. However, B was rejected for large east shipments (REQ-2440, REQ-2448), a south invoice (REQ-2465), and east claims (REQ-2467–2469). Refund context currently supports B more than urgency/follow-up alone.
- Claims remain unresolved: B is specifically unsafe for the tested east claims; no reliable alternative is established. Invoice routing is also unresolved after B failed for REQ-2465.
- Omitted/truncated option text does not necessarily mean unavailable: D was accepted despite omission/truncation. Still inspect the complete current option list.
- Avoid routing solely by region, size, urgency, department, sender, or wording. Prefer explicit workflow rules; absent a rule, collect outcomes rather than guess.
